headline: Extends the FTC's authority to fight internet fraud that crosses national borders through fiscal year 2027 and requires the agency to report on that work.
what_it_does: The law extends the U.S. SAFE WEB Act of 2006 through fiscal year 2027. That Act lets the Federal Trade Commission take certain actions against online fraud and deception that involve other countries. The law also requires the FTC to report on its cross-border online fraud work and to recommend policy changes to address it.

who_it_affects.group: Consumers who shop or do business online with people or companies in other countries
who_it_affects.how: The FTC keeps its authority to act against cross-border online fraud and deception that could affect them.
The agency's cross-border enforcement authority is extended, and it must prepare a report with policy recommendations on online fraud.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on October 20, 2020, and the extended authority runs through fiscal year 2027.
